texto_para_tela: "DID NOT SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE PAIN OR SYSTEMIC EFFECTS"
credito_sugerido: Source: Isbister et al., Annals of Emergency Medicine, 2014 (RAVE-II)
nota: F177 relido no resumo do RAVE-II (224 pacientes randomizados). PENDENTE f160, ACHADO: o 'estudo pequeno de 2003' é Isbister & Gray, MJA 2003;179(2):88–91 (NÃO o arquivo fontes/a/mja2003-redback.*, que é a carta de Wiener, MJA 179(8):455–456, sobre esse estudo). O estudo: '68 people with definite redback spider bites … (1 February 1999 to 30 April 2002)'; 'One of six patients treated with intramuscular antivenom (17%) had no pain at 24 hours, compared with two of 17 untreated patients (12%) (difference, 5%; 95% CI, -36% to +64%; P = 0.95)'; conclusão: 'Intramuscular antivenom appears to be less effective than previously thought and its use by this route needs review'. No texto: 'redback spider antivenom was introduced without controlled studies to demonstrate efficacy or safety'. Seis tratados contra 17: pequeno de fato. Na tela, se for: 'A SMALL 2003 STUDY: 6 TREATED, 17 NOT · NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE', com 'Source: Isbister & Gray, Medical Journal of Australia, 2003'.

texto_aprovado: A later trial, though, found that the antivenom didn't significantly ease pain or other symptoms. So it isn't clear that the antivenom is what keeps redback bites from killing.
